name: Russian
intro: Learn Cyrillic first and keep lexical stress in vocabulary notes. Stress is mobile and often unpredictable; unstressed vowels can reduce. Hard and soft consonants contrast. Stress marks in teaching material are aids and are generally absent in ordinary Russian. Professional ability requires a broad lexicon and accurate aspect and case choices, not only reading an alphabet.

foundation.name: Russian
notes: Several Cyrillic letters look Latin but have different values: В is /v/, Н /n/, Р /r/, С /s/, У /u/, Х /x/. Ъ and Ь have no independent vowel sound. Practise recognising them inside words, not only reciting the order.

Stress is lexical and can move under inflection. Mark it while learning: вода́, во́ды. Unstressed vowels reduce in ordinary speech. Many consonants contrast hard and soft; following е/ё/и/ю/я or ь often signals softness. ы is a separate vowel requiring listening practice.
ё is often printed as е, but its pronunciation and stress must still be learned. Word-final voiced obstruents generally devoice. Use a dictionary recording for a new word and its inflected forms.
building: книга → книги → книгу = book → of a book → a book as a direct object. Endings express case and number; they are not interchangeable suffix decorations.
читать → прочитать = read as an activity → read through / finish reading. Prefixes can change aspect and lexical meaning, so record the pair with an example.
Я читаю книгу. = I am reading a book. Я не читаю книгу. = I am not reading a book. Russian generally has no present-tense copula in a simple identity sentence: Это книга. = This is a book.

sections.title: Cases, agreement and prepositions
sections.explanation: Russian has six main cases. Nominative marks many subjects, genitive possession and quantities, dative recipients, accusative many objects, instrumental means or roles, and prepositional certain governed complements. Animate masculine/plural accusative often resembles genitive. Adjectives and pronouns agree in gender, number and case. Learn prepositions with their meanings and case: в + accusative can mark destination; в + prepositional location. Many verbs govern a case independently of English structure.
examples: I am reading a new book.
Location with в and prepositional case.
exercises: Distinguish в Москву and в Москве.
To Moscow is a destination; in Moscow is a location. The case expresses the relation.
What belongs on a noun card?
Gender, stress, plural and difficult case forms, with an example.

sections.title: Aspect and temporal perspective
sections.explanation: Imperfective often presents an activity, habit or process; perfective presents a bounded whole or achieved result. These are perspectives rather than a simple finished/unfinished test. Читать and прочитать form a useful reading contrast. Perfective nonpast forms normally express future meaning; imperfective has present and a compound future with быть. Past forms agree in gender and number, not person: читал, читала, читали. Negation, repetition and expectation affect aspect choice.
examples: Perfective presents a bounded reading event.
exercises: Can every English past tense be translated with perfective?
No. Perspective, repetition and context determine aspect.
How does a female speaker say I was reading?
Я читала. The past form marks feminine gender.

sections.title: Motion, modality and impersonal sentences
sections.explanation: Russian distinguishes unidirectional and multidirectional or habitual motion in pairs such as идти/ходить and ехать/ездить. Transport and walking also differ. Prefixes add direction and often change aspectual relationships; learn the complete pair in context. Мне нужно ... and мне нравится ... use dative experiencers. Modal expressions may be impersonal, so an English subject does not always become Russian nominative.
examples: I am going to the library on foot.
I need to check the data.
Dative experiencer with an impersonal necessity expression.
exercises: Contrast я иду and я хожу in a suitable context.
Иду can be one directed current journey; хожу can describe a habitual activity or non-unidirectional motion.
Translate I like this method.
Мне нравится этот метод. Метод is the grammatical subject.

sections.title: Participles, clauses and academic compression
sections.explanation: Russian formal prose uses participles to modify nouns and adverbial participles to relate actions. Agreement identifies the noun modified; the implied agent of an adverbial participle normally matches the relevant clause subject. A literal English dangling construction can produce a Russian error too. Relative который agrees with the antecedent in gender and number, while its case follows its role within the relative clause.
examples: Passive past participle agrees with данные.
Relative pronoun is the object within its clause.
exercises: What should you identify before translating a participial phrase?
The head noun, agreement, agent, time relation and any governed complements.
Expand данные, полученные вчера.
Данные, которые были получены вчера. A finite relative makes the passive event explicit.

sections.title: Professional register and reading
sections.explanation:
Use Вы for polite address, with conventions determined by relationship and medium. Не могли бы Вы ... is a standard courteous request. Distinguish возможно, вероятно and несомненно rather than translating all as probably.
Teaching passage: Результаты исследования указывают на связь между двумя факторами. Однако они не доказывают, что один фактор вызывает другой. Для более точного вывода необходимо учитывать условия исследования.
Translation: The study results indicate an association between two factors. However, they do not prove that one causes the other. A more precise conclusion requires considering the study conditions.
examples: Не могли бы Вы уточнить этот пункт?
Однако это не доказывает причинную связь.
However, this does not prove a causal relationship.
Contrast and an explicit limit on inference.
exercises: Summarise the passage without strengthening the claim.
It reports an association but not proof of causation, and requires attention to conditions.
Write a 100-word clarification request.
Use accurate cases, appropriate Вы address, a precise question and a practical next step.

rules.title: Subject pronouns
rules.explanation: Subject pronouns distinguish person and number. Вы can address one person politely or multiple people. Russian often omits the present copula in identity and classification statements.

examples.native: Ты должен сделать своих родителей счастливыми.
examples.translation: You must make your parents happy.
Will you tell Tom?

examples.native: Я хочу выполнить план любой ценой.
examples.translation: I want to execute the plan by all means.

rules.title: Object and oblique pronouns
rules.explanation: Pronouns have case-specific forms, and several cases share a surface form. Identify the governing verb/preposition and intended relationship rather than translating by word order alone.

examples.native: Тебя, по идее, здесь быть не должно.
examples.translation: You're not supposed to be here.
We need to test it.
I think you should wait for us.

rules.title: Dative pronouns
rules.explanation: Dative often marks a recipient or experiencer. Impersonal constructions such as Мне холодно use dative where English uses a subject plus be.

examples.native: Тебе не кажется, что это слишком далеко зашло?
examples.translation: Don't you think this has gone far enough?

examples.native: Мне в целом нравится китайская еда.
examples.translation: I like Chinese food in general.
Please peel this orange for me.

rules.title: Possessive forms
rules.explanation: Possessive adjectives agree with the possessed noun in case, gender and number. The possessor’s sex does not choose мой versus моя.

examples.translation: My mother is beautiful.
Is your wife still in America?

examples.native: Мне только что звонила ваша учительница.
examples.translation: I just got a call from your teacher.

rules.title: Locative prepositions
rules.explanation: Prepositions govern case. В/на commonly distinguish destination with accusative and location with prepositional. У + genitive is frequent in possession; с has more than one case/meaning pattern.

examples.translation: Go talk to them.
None of them are busy.

examples.native: Том встретил Мэри сегодня утром по дороге в школу.
examples.translation: Tom met Mary this morning on his way to school.

rules.title: Adjective agreement
rules.explanation: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender, number and case. Short and long adjective forms have distinct distributions and meanings. Learn a full phrase, not an isolated ending.

examples.translation: The storm did great harm to the crop.
Tom already has a new girlfriend.
The mathematics class is good.

rules.title: Past forms of быть
rules.explanation: Russian past tense generally agrees in gender and number rather than person. Был/была/было/были are forms of be and can establish a past state or accompany another construction.

examples.translation: Tom was scared to death.
Tom also was very hungry.
I think you were right.

rules.title: Common present verbs
rules.explanation: Present forms agree with person and number. Ordinary present-time activity uses an imperfective verb. Perfective forms with similar endings normally refer to future events.

examples.translation: I think that'll happen someday.
Tom doesn't know much.

examples.native: Том никогда не думает о других.
examples.translation: Tom never thinks about others.

rules.title: Bounded past and aspect
rules.explanation: These common perfective past forms present a bounded event in suitable contexts. Aspect is lexical and interacts with negation and discourse; a prefix is not always a simple completion switch.

examples.native: Она сказала, что не будет ждать.
examples.translation: She said she wouldn't wait.

examples.native: Даже Том такого бы не сделал.
examples.translation: Even Tom wouldn't do that.

examples.native: Ты не в ответе за то, что сделал Том.
examples.translation: You aren't responsible for what Tom did.

rules.title: Future constructions
rules.explanation: Буду plus an imperfective infinitive expresses future activity. A perfective verb can form its future without буду. Буду alone can also mean will be.

examples.translation: I'll keep my fingers crossed.

examples.native: "На пикнике будет живая музыка". - "Что за музыка?"
examples.translation: "There will be live music at the picnic." "What kind of music?"
I will be very careful.

rules.title: Motion forms
rules.explanation: Motion verbs distinguish travel on foot/vehicle and directed versus multidirectional/habitual patterns. Prefixes add direction and other meanings. The English verb go hides distinctions Russian expresses.

examples.native: Он пошёл домой через три часа.
examples.translation: He went home three hours later.
I was on my way home.
I don't wear shoes in my house.

rules.title: Negation
rules.explanation: Не negates a predicate or constituent; нет states absence/existence negation and commonly governs genitive. Negative pronouns can participate in negative concord. Нельзя can express prohibition or impossibility.

examples.translation: Fish don't like sunlight.
Tom didn't have to explain anything.
Tom isn't lazy.

rules.title: Modal and impersonal words
rules.explanation: Modality can be expressed with verbs or impersonal predicates. Нужно/надо often combine with a dative experiencer and infinitive. Может can also be a verb meaning can; context distinguishes inference.

examples.translation: Tom needs attention.

examples.native: Тому нужно, чтобы Мэри кто-нибудь помог.
examples.translation: Tom needs somebody to help Mary.
I thought it might be you.

rules.title: Questions
rules.explanation: Где asks location, куда destination, откуда source. Question words can inflect for case. Word order and intonation help mark a question without an English do auxiliary.

examples.translation: When can we go swimming?

examples.native: Том, вероятно, думал, что я счастлив.
examples.translation: Tom probably thought I was happy.
Where's the nearest pizzeria?

rules.title: Content clauses
rules.explanation: Что can introduce reported content, while чтобы often marks purpose or a desired event. Ли helps form indirect yes/no questions. Identical words may have interrogative or relative roles elsewhere.

examples.native: Том приехал сюда, чтобы учить французский.
examples.translation: Tom came here to study French.

examples.native: Том использовал лом, чтобы открыть крышку ящика.
examples.translation: Tom used a crowbar to pry open the lid of the crate.

examples.native: Том хотел, чтобы они оба ушли.
examples.translation: Tom wanted both of them to leave.

rules.title: Relative forms
rules.explanation: Который agrees with its antecedent for gender/number but takes case from its role inside the relative clause. Do not copy the antecedent’s case automatically.

examples.native: Первым предметом, который он приобрёл, стал будильник.
examples.translation: The first item he bought was an alarm clock.

examples.native: Есть математическое понятие, которого я не понимаю. Не могли бы вы мне его объяснить?
examples.translation: There's a mathematical concept that I don't understand. Could you explain it to me?

examples.native: Экзолуна - это луна, которая вращается вокруг экзопланеты.
examples.translation: An exomoon is a moon that orbits around an exoplanet.

rules.title: Hypothetical бы
rules.explanation: Бы combines with a past-form verb to express a conditional/subjunctive meaning. Past morphology here does not always locate the situation in the past. Если introduces an if condition.

examples.translation: You would've liked her.
I wish I had Tom's brains.

examples.native: О чём бы вы хотели поговорить?
examples.translation: What would you like to talk about?

rules.title: Logical connectors
rules.explanation: Distinguish cause, concession and result. Поэтому presents a consequence, not its cause. Несмотря often belongs to a prepositional concessive construction requiring its own complement.

examples.native: Есть только одна религия, хотя у неё сотня вариаций.
examples.translation: There is only one religion, though there are a hundred versions of it.

examples.native: Он не извинился, хотя и был неправ.
examples.translation: Although he was wrong, he didn't say he was sorry.

examples.native: Так как автобуса не было, мне пришлось идти пешком.
examples.translation: Since there was no bus, I had to walk.

rules.title: Quantity and comparison
rules.explanation: Numerals govern distinctive noun forms, with patterns for 1, 2–4 and other numbers. Gender can affect два/две. Comparatives such as лучше can be invariant in relevant uses.

examples.native: Она оказалась меньше, чем я себе её представлял.
examples.translation: She turned out to be smaller than I'd thought she was.

examples.native: Том и Мария больше не любят друг друга.
examples.translation: Tom and Mary don't love each other anymore.
Tom ate more than I did.

rules.title: Professional stance and courtesy
rules.explanation: Пожалуйста supports courteous requests. Возможно/вероятно limit certainty; следует/необходимо express recommendations or necessity. Distinguish a documented claim from a possibility.

examples.translation: Leave him alone, please.
Please come again.
Please move the desk to the left.

passages.title: Learning with a clear purpose
passages.native: Я изучаю новый язык. Каждый день я читаю короткий текст и слушаю понятные примеры. Я записываю полезные слова в тетрадь. Когда я делаю ошибку, я проверяю правило и пробую ещё раз. Моя цель — понимать людей и ясно выражать свои мысли.
passages.translation: I am learning a new language. Each day, I read a short text and listen to clear examples. I write useful words in a notebook. When I make a mistake, I check the rule and try again. My goal is to understand people and express my ideas clearly.

grammarTerms: Noun
A word naming a person, thing or idea: student, book, freedom.
Verb
A word describing an action or state: read, know, be.
Subject
The participant linked to the main verb’s subject pattern. In The student reads a book, the student is the subject.
Object
A participant selected by a verb. In The student reads a book, a book is the direct object.
Agreement
One word changes to match another, for example an adjective matching a noun’s gender and number.
Case
A noun/pronoun form marking its relationship in a sentence. Cases can mark subjects, objects, possession or relations usually expressed by English prepositions.
Gender
A grammatical noun class. It does not always describe the sex of a person or any physical property.
Tense
A verb system that relates a situation to a time, often past or non-past.
Aspect
How a situation is viewed: unfolding, completed, habitual, experienced or in a resulting state.
Infinitive
A non-finite verb form often used for a dictionary entry or a complement. It does not by itself give the ordinary person/tense pattern.
Participle
A verb-derived form used in compound predicates or as a modifier; its exact function depends on the language and construction.
Clause
A unit organised around a predicate. One sentence can contain several clauses.
Register
Language choices suited to a situation: casual conversation, polite requests, academic writing or another context.
